reasoning:
I need to figure out which JSON edits to make for the annotator prompt and memory policy around demo_placements and goal_target—specifically adding the real-carry entry condition, excluding artifacts, and concretely defining the stable set within the existing release/entry description.

For the goal_target rule, I want to sharpen the logic so it applies to any single frame, even when the overall layout appears unchanged: matching positions mean no movement, while two unmatched positions identify the movers who swap places. I'll apply the same clarification to the policy memory side and draft the exact quoted edits.

edits.modify_from: a release is a frame where the fingers open from ~46% to ~100% right after frames where that cube was 'held in the gripper'; decide by nearest match within a few pixels which target of the STABLE demo target set (the four positions that stay the same through the demo) the cube now rests on,
edits.modify_to: first find the STABLE target set: the four target positions listed in the demo frames where the goal-named cube is held raised and carried toward the image centre just before the final centre release (cube left near [82, 127]); every entry you write is one of those four positions, to the pixel. A release is a frame where the fingers open from ~46% to ~100% right after frames where that cube was 'held in the gripper', and it counts only if it ends a real carry: frames labelled held with the gripper raised (height about 0.15) and the cube moving away from where it last rested, then the gripper lowered to table height and the fingers opening. A frame with fingers partly open (~39-46%) and the cube labelled held at table height on the very spot it already rested on, with no raised carry before it, is an artifact (it happens right after a button press, where the fingers were 0% open) and is NOT a placement; a re-grasp that lifts and sets the cube back on the same target without resting elsewhere is NOT a placement either. For each counted release decide by nearest match within a few pixels which stable target the cube now rests on,

edits.modify_from: Never write values from the opening frames, from release frames, or from the final parked frames.
edits.modify_to: Never write values from the opening frames, from release frames, or from the final parked frames, even if they differ from the stable position by only a pixel or two; a target never gets two entries for one carry.
e.g. releases on [107, 166], then [125, 119], then [97, 88], then a button press, a spurious 39%-open frame over [97, 88], then the centre carry: [[107, 166], [125, 119], [97, 88]]

edits.modify_from: If every parked frame lists the same four positions as the stable set within a few pixels, nothing moved: write the target listed in the scene at the start of execution nearest the ordinal entry. If some parked frame lists positions matching no stable target, exactly two stable targets are missing from it: those two are the movers, and they swap places, each ending at the other's original spot.
edits.modify_to: Check each parked frame one at a time. Only if EVERY parked frame lists the same four positions as the stable set within a few pixels did nothing move: then write the target listed in the scene at the start of execution nearest the ordinal entry. If ANY single parked frame lists a position matching no stable target within a few pixels, the two stable targets absent from that frame are the movers, and they have swapped places, each ending at the other's original spot. Apply this even if the last parked frames and the scene at the start of execution again list four positions within a few pixels of the stable set: a swap ends with the movers on each other's old spots, so an unchanged-looking final layout is NOT evidence that nothing moved.
